A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 13C-NMRSpectra are a powerful tool in the investigation of the composition of mutarotation equilibria of 6-substituted and 6,4-substituted Amadori compounds.
we have shown that the 13C-NMRS of the C-1, C-4, C-5, and C-6 carbons of the aldoses are sensitive to the presence of the C-2 epimeric center and to the presence of a C-6 substituent.
the mutarotation of 6-substituted Amadori compounds (1, 2, 4, and 6) is much slower than that of the 4, 6-disubstituted compounds (3 and 5) and the unsubstituted compound 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-6 and C-4 hydroxyl groups are involved in hydrogen bonding with solvent molecules in the solid state.
the mutarotations equilibria of C-6-modified Amadori compounds (1-6) are strongly influenced by the nature of substituents at C-6 and C-4 and C-6 of the carbohydrate moiety.
